name: metrunio
description: Read your Metrunio measurement: conversions, revenue, channels and customer journeys. Read-only.

interface.longDescription:
Metrunio is first-party conversion tracking and attribution for online shops and lead websites, hosted in the EU. This plugin lets ChatGPT read the same numbers you see in the Metrunio portal, so you can ask about your marketing in plain language.

Ask how many orders or enquiries you had, which channels and campaigns they are attributed to, how revenue developed over time, how attribution models compare, or what a single customer journey looked like. It also reads commerce figures (contribution margin, new customers, products), web analytics (visits, sources, technology) and the answers to your post-purchase question. Every answer names the attribution model, the period and the time zone it was calculated with, and separates measured numbers from attributed ones. If data is missing, the plugin says so instead of filling the gap.

Before reading too much into a drop, ask about data quality: it shows whether a change is real or a measurement problem.

All eleven tools are read-only. The plugin cannot change settings, campaigns or data.

Requirements: a Metrunio account. Which figures the plugin can read depends on the account; the help article on connecting AI tools explains the details. An administrator of the account approves the connection on Metrunio's consent page and can disconnect it at any time under "AI tools".
capabilities: Read conversions and revenue for any period
Break results down by channel, campaign or source
Show revenue and conversions over time
Compare attribution models for the same period
List individual conversions with their attribution
Look up a customer journey and its touchpoints
Check data quality before interpreting a change
Read contribution margin, new customers and products
Read visits, sources and technology from web analytics
Read the answers to the post-purchase question
Answer questions about Metrunio from the help centre
defaultPrompt: How many conversions and how much revenue did I have in the last 30 days?
Which channel was attributed the most revenue last month?
Is my measurement complete, or is something missing?

positive.prompt: How many conversions and how much revenue did I have in the last 30 days?
positive.expected_behavior: Answers with measured conversions, revenue before and after refunds and attributed conversions for the last 30 days, naming the attribution model, the period and the time zone. Numbers equal the overview in the Metrunio portal for the same period.

positive.prompt: Which channel was attributed the most revenue last month?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists channels with attributed revenue and conversions for last month, sorted by revenue, and names the model. If the month started before measurement began, says that it is only partly measured.

positive.prompt: Show me revenue per week for the last 12 weeks.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns weekly revenue and conversions for twelve weeks with the time zone; weeks without data are shown as zero or missing, not interpolated, and weeks before measurement began are marked as incomplete.

positive.prompt: How would last month look under first touch compared with last click?
positive.expected_behavior: Compares attributed revenue per channel for both models over the same period and explains that the attributed total stays the same and only its distribution changes.

positive.description: Data quality before interpreting a drop
positive.prompt: Revenue dropped yesterday. Is that real or a tracking problem?
positive.expected_behavior: Checks the measurement status (processed and rejected events, processing backlog, open findings) and compares yesterday with earlier days before interpreting the drop, then says whether it looks real, like a measurement problem, or that it cannot tell.

negative.description: Write request: the plugin is read-only
negative.prompt: Pause my Google Ads campaign Summer Sale.
Estimate how much revenue I would have had if consent had been 100 percent.

negative.description: Personal data: no names or email addresses
negative.prompt: Give me the names and email addresses of the people who bought last week.

de-DE.subtitle: Messdaten und Attribution
de-DE.description:
Metrunio misst Conversions und ordnet sie zu, für Onlineshops und Websites mit Anfragen, betrieben in der EU. Mit diesem Plugin liest ChatGPT dieselben Zahlen, die du im Metrunio-Portal siehst, und du fragst in deinen eigenen Worten.

Frag, wie viele Bestellungen oder Anfragen du hattest, welchen Kanälen und Kampagnen sie zugeordnet sind, wie sich der Umsatz entwickelt hat, wie sich Attributionsmodelle unterscheiden oder wie eine einzelne Customer Journey verlief. Dazu liest es Handelszahlen (Deckungsbeitrag, Neukunden, Produkte), Webanalyse (Besuche, Quellen, Technik) und die Antworten auf deine Nachkauf-Frage. Jede Antwort nennt Attributionsmodell, Zeitraum und Zeitzone und trennt gemessene von zugeordneten Zahlen. Fehlen Daten, sagt das Plugin das, statt die Lücke zu füllen.

Bevor du einen Rückgang deutest, frag nach der Datenqualität: Sie zeigt, ob die Änderung echt ist oder ein Messproblem.

Alle elf Werkzeuge lesen nur. Das Plugin kann keine Einstellungen, Kampagnen oder Daten ändern.

Voraussetzung: ein Metrunio-Konto. Welche Zahlen das Plugin lesen kann, hängt vom Konto ab; die Einzelheiten stehen im Hilfeartikel zum Anbinden von KI-Werkzeugen. Eine Administration des Kontos gibt die Verbindung auf der Freigabeseite von Metrunio frei und trennt sie jederzeit unter „KI-Werkzeuge“.
